findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-FENG-24.result.json: item 60 (Lemma 5.7), items 62–64, E41.correction and route ShtukaTateCohomologyAndGlobalBaseChange
findings.claim: Lemma 5.7 identifies the whole fixed scheme with descended H-shtukas even for ramified X′/X. Killing automorphisms makes the equivariance cocycle unique but does not make it effective descent along a ramified cover. The current extraction and the accepted component repair still rely on this false identification.
findings.evidence: Published version, §5.1.7 pp.32–33 permits arbitrary cyclic degree-p extensions, and Lemma 5.7 p.37 concludes that a cocycle is “equivalent to a descent datum”. Take p=3, X=P¹_t over F_7, X′=P¹_u with t=u³ and σ(u)=2u, H=G_m and G=Res_{X′/X}G_m. Choose no legs, D empty and x_0=(t=1). The trivial line bundle on X′ with Frobenius identity and level frame u modulo (u³−1)^n is fixed for every n: the frame changes to 2u, and multiplication by 4 identifies it with the original frame, with 4³=1. Its framed automorphisms are trivial. It lies in the degree-zero HN piece. It is not pulled back from a framed line bundle on X: pullback degree forces that line bundle to be trivial, and its level frame would be invariant, whereas no constant multiple of u is invariant even at n=1. The unique linearization acts nontrivially at u=0. This counterexample persists at all depths at x_0. The author PDF, p.38, has the same argument. The report gives the complete construction and precise scope.
findings.fix: Add a source issue for ramified descent and replace item 60 by a correctly qualified statement: either an étale-cover theorem or the locus with effective descent/trivial inertia, with the descent criterion proved. If ramified covers must be handled by adding level at branch places, specify sufficient level at every branch place and prove that it enforces effective descent. Revisit the whole-fixed-locus localization and E41 component repair, propagating the corrected hypotheses through route 2 and the local applications in route 3. Do not claim that the main existence-of-base-change theorem is disproved; the counterexample concerns the asserted fixed-locus identification at the stated level.

findings.claim: Fusion isomorphisms and their composition compatibility alone do not imply the excursion relations. Item 56 quantifies over arbitrary ordinary functors and omits even preservation of zero morphisms, so its claimed construction of an excursion action is false under its written axioms.
findings.evidence: Published p.33 states precisely two admissibility conditions and allows A to be any ring. Even after correcting E35, take A=k and for every finite I take the constant functor H_I with value k, trivial Γ^I-action, and every morphism sent to id_k. Identity fusion maps satisfy both stated conditions, including empty I. The Construction 5.2 composite is then id_k even when x=0. But §2.4.2(iii), pp.11–12, and item 13 require linearity in x, hence S_{I,W,0,ξ,(γ_i)}=0. Choose W=1 so every map is an L-group morphism; this obstruction is independent of finding 3.
findings.fix: Specify a coefficient-compatible additive/k-linear functor contract (with the corresponding k-action on the target category), then state and prove the additional normalization, inflation and coherence conditions needed for all six excursion relations. In particular test zero creation, scalar multiples and sums. If using an existing geometric construction, formulate the abstraction around its actual operations and prove their relations; do not infer them solely from fusion. Record the missing hypotheses as a source issue distinct from the already repaired index swap E35.

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-FENG-24.result.json: item 56 creation/annihilation arrows; item 13 input convention; route ShtukaTateCohomologyAndGlobalBaseChange
findings.claim: The creation and annihilation maps in item 56 need only be invariant under the diagonal dual group, but the functor to which they are applied is defined on representations of the full L-group. Such maps need not be morphisms in that domain, even if the missing linearity in finding 2 is added.
findings.evidence: Construction 5.2, published p.33, applies H_{ {0} }(x) while its parenthesis identifies x only as a G-hat-equivariant map. Let p=3, G=G_m split and Γ the Weil group of a function field with a nontrivial unramified quadratic character χ (degree modulo 2). Put W=k(χ), trivial under G-hat, and I={0}. The vector x=1 and dual vector ξ=1 satisfy the stated diagonal-G-hat invariance. But x:1→W is not an L G=G-hat×Γ morphism: a γ with χ(γ)=−1 sends x to −x. Thus H_{ {0} }(x) is undefined. The same defect is present for ξ. Proposition 5.12(i), p.39, instead works with functors on geometric representations, pointing to the distinction that the abstract contract must preserve.
findings.fix: Separate the geometric Rep_k(G-hat^I) functors and their Galois-equivariant/descent structure, so creation and annihilation are defined before requiring arithmetic equivariance, and explicitly construct the excursion action for the full L-group presentation. Alternatively give a valid induction/auxiliary-representation construction for the non-Galois-invariant vectors and prove independence and the relations. Do not simply require full L-group invariance of x and ξ: that would discard allowed generators of item 13. Add the one-dimensional quadratic-character example as a domain/type test, and record the source-level typing defect.

findings.claim: The review-added tor-amplitude statement assigns Rj_* a bound of twice the relative dimension. For an open immersion this bound is zero, yet Rj_* need not be t-exact. This is a new false strengthening introduced by the extraction review.
findings.evidence: Item rev-6 asserts that both Rf_! and Rj_* take tor-amplitude [a,b] into [a,b+c] with c bounded by twice the relative dimension. Take j:G_m→A¹ over an algebraic closure of F_7 and A=k[C_3], k=Fbar_3. The constant free A-sheaf has tor-amplitude [0,0], and j has relative dimension zero. Nevertheless (R¹j_*A)_0 is nonzero: on the punctured strict henselian trait, z³=t is a nontrivial Kummer torsor because the valuation of t is 1, not divisible by 3. The class persists for k and for its free A-summand. Therefore Rj_*A cannot have tor-amplitude [0,0]. Feng p.16 only invokes preservation of finite tor-amplitude; Stacks tag 0F10 states finiteness of cohomological dimension, not this relative-dimension estimate.
findings.fix: Separate the Rf_! and Rj_* statements. Retain the appropriate relative-dimension bound for compactly supported pushforward with its hypotheses, but give Rj_* a valid finite cohomological/tor-amplitude bound depending on the ambient geometry, or retain only preservation of finiteness if that is all the consumer needs. Add the punctured-line stalk test. Attribute the false numeric bound to rev-6, not to Feng or Stacks; retain the useful preservation theorem and its existing owner.
